title: Triage review of c43's CIPS consumer on fresh seed 57: the pack numbers replicate (consumer 30 persistent splits, generation 3; prey 76, generation 9), but 27 of 28 consumer splits coincide with a prey split, the consumers are bands on prey edges (median 88% of frames touching prey), and no consumer track lives half the run
summary: Labkit re-run of the claim's world.py unchanged on fresh seed 57 at the claim's settings (128^2, --frames 120 --lineage-k 5, t=12000); it ran at the default step without a crash. Consumer species: about 32 bodies, 30 persistent splits, generation 3, merge/split 0.09, 0 persistent tracks (longest track of any kind 40 frames = 4000 t). Prey: 76 persistent splits, generation 9, merge/split 0.06. c55's pairtest.py (K 5): 27 of 28 persistent consumer splits coincide with a prey split; consumers touch prey in a median 88% of frames; 7 consumer tracks last >= 20 frames, and 3 of them touch >= 2 unrelated prey. The sheet and tracks.png show white consumer bars lying along the edges of blue prey droplets and dividing when the droplet pinches; free consumer dots are rare. I did not run the consumer-free twin or the prey-removal fork.

observations.S: rerun/seed57/sheet.png t=0: unstructured field; prey droplets with consumer bands by t=500

seeds_run.result: pass for the numbers (consumer 30 persistent splits, gen 3; prey 76, gen 9); weak for I and D as the consumer's own

verdicts.limitation: I and D of the consumer are not its own on my seed. The consumer is a band on the edge of its prey droplet (median 88% of frames touching prey; tracks.png #61, #412, #585). It divides when the droplet pinches: 27 of 28 persistent consumer splits coincide with a prey split (pairtest_s57.json). No consumer or prey track lives half of the run (longest 40 of 120 frames). This is the same pair co-division that the reviewers of c52's and c60's digestion ecology found. I did not run the matched twin or the fork, so X and E are not checked.
